scope.flow: Distributor.addRewards updates pending-reward accounting before the external transferFrom, allowing a malicious token to re-enter claimRewards during transferFrom
scope.environment: Solidity smart contract (Distributor.sol) with external token transferFrom interaction
evidence: Reentrancy / accounting before transfer in Distributor.addRewards — attacker can re-enter and observe/act on updated accounting

Distributor.addRewards updates internal pending-reward accounting before performing the external transferFrom call. A malicious token can re-enter during transferFrom and call claimRewards (or other entrypoints) while accounting has already been increased, producing a clear reentrancy window that can be used for griefing and, in some scenarios, monetary extraction.

Attackers can force the code path to re-enter claimRewards during addRewards, demonstrating an exploitable reentrancy window. This enables griefing and may be combined with other weaknesses to steal tokens.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the attacker is an authorized caller of addRewards or claimRewards; no explicit permissionless-call statement.
Report does not establish a concrete prior accounting state before addRewards; the increased accounting is produced by the checked action itself.
Monetary extraction is described as conditional ('in some scenarios', 'may be combined'), not a definite outcome.
Unauthorized forced liquidation/withdrawal is conditional on future auth-check changes in upgrades.
Direct ability to manipulate reward accounting and to re-enter core flows is High states a severity/ability, not a distinct harmful outcome.
